title: Global IoT Sensor Telemetry Aggregation
business: A smart-city infrastructure provider managing millions of connected traffic sensors that generate high-velocity time-series data.
problem: The existing relational database infrastructure suffers from write-contention and schema rigidity when attempting to ingest concurrent telemetry streams from geographically dispersed sensors, leading to data loss during peak traffic hours.
solution: Amazon Keyspaces provides a serverless, Apache Cassandra-compatible database that scales horizontally to handle high-volume write throughput. By utilizing a wide-column store, the system allows for flexible schema evolution as new sensor types are deployed, ensuring that incoming telemetry is persisted without the overhead of managing database clusters or manual sharding.
steps: Define a keyspace with a replication strategy suited for the required regional availability.
Create tables using CQL, ensuring the partition key is chosen to distribute sensor data evenly across the cluster.
Configure the application driver to connect to the Keyspaces endpoint using standard Cassandra-compatible drivers.
Implement asynchronous write operations to handle the high-velocity ingestion of sensor telemetry.
Monitor table capacity and throughput using CloudWatch to ensure the provisioned or on-demand settings align with traffic patterns.
outcome: The architecture achieves seamless ingestion of high-velocity telemetry data with consistent write performance, allowing the city to maintain real-time traffic monitoring without manual database scaling interventions.
limitation: A primary limitation is the lack of support for complex multi-table joins or ACID transactions across multiple partitions. To verify this, developers should review the query execution plans and ensure data modeling follows denormalization patterns rather than relational normalization.

The requirement to manually shard the database cluster.
